newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were narrowly mixed in moderate trade, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said most traders were sidelined before today's issue of the U.S. March consumer price index and business inventories data. The consumer price index for March is forecast to show a gain of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.3 percent increase reported in February.
March business inventories are expected to show an increase of 0.2 percent against February's 0.1 percent gain.

"Rates were narrowly mixed this morning on some position adjustments. Basically, everyone is waiting for today's issue of the CPI and retail sales figures for fresh clues to market direction," a local dealer said.

"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions, so I don't think there will be much impact unless the figures are way off market expectations," he said.
In short dates, Tuesday/Wednesday and Wednesday/Thursday rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, respectively.
Among term rates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent and four-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16.
Nine-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent and twelve-months rose 1/8 point to 6-7/16 6-5/16 percent.
